太后 is Cao herself, the biography’s subject; 唯太后恩顧不衰 means imperial favor toward her never waned, not favor conferred by a third-party empress dowager.
At that time consorts and attendants filled the chambers, and Lady Cao rarely gained access to the imperial bed, yet the Empress Dowager's gracious favor toward her never waned.
At that time consorts and attendants filled the chambers, and she rarely gained access to the imperial bed, yet gracious favor toward the Empress Dowager never waned.
The same clause makes Cao (太后) the recipient of 恩顧, matching later units where 太后 is Cao; the original English treats the title as a separate person conferring favor.

伯仲 is a sibling-closeness metaphor; both speakers are women, so “brother” missexes them.
